title: Getting around
goal: Ask for and follow directions, take a rickshaw or bus, and give polite and informal instructions.
intro: The auto-rickshaw (**રિક્ષા**) is the classic way to get around Gujarati cities, along with city buses and Ahmedabad's BRTS and metro. This unit teaches the **imperative** — how to tell someone to go, stop or turn — in its intimate, polite and extra-polite forms, plus the case endings for 'to', 'from' and 'up to'.

vocab.en: to get off/out; to go down
to sit; to get on (a vehicle)
up to, until, as far as

vocab.note: n · બસ (f) 'bus' is spelled like બસ 'enough'; the state bus is ઍસ.ટી. 'S.T.'
f · Ahmedabad's river is the સાબરમતી

phrases.en: Excuse me, where is the station?
How far is it from here?
Bhai, will you go to Manek Chowk? (to a rickshaw driver)
How much will the fare be?
Does this bus go to Gandhinagar?

phrases.native: મારે આવતા સ્ટૉપ પર ઊતરવું છે.
phrases.roman: māre āvtā sṭop par ūtarvuṃ chhe.
phrases.en: I want to get off at the next stop.

grammar.title: The imperative: three levels
grammar.body:
Gujarati commands change with the level of politeness:

**Intimate (તું):** bare stem — **જા** 'go', **આવ** 'come', **બેસ** 'sit', **વળ** 'turn'.
**Polite (તમે):** stem + **-ઓ** — **જાઓ, આવો, બેસો, વળો**. This is the normal form with adults.
**Deferred / extra polite:** stem + **-જો** — **જજો, આવજો, બેસજો, વળજો**. It sounds softer and often refers to later ('do turn right when you get there'). Intimate version: **-જે** (આવજે).

Negative commands use **ના / ન** before the verb, or the -શો + નહીં form for politeness: **ત્યાં ના જાઓ** 'don't go there', **ચિંતા કરશો નહીં** 'please don't worry'.

examples.en: Turn right at the second lane. (polite, deferred)

grammar.title: Direction and location: -એ, -થી, સુધી, તરફ
grammar.body:
Gujarati usually needs **no word for 'to'** with places: **હું બજાર જાઉં છું** 'I'm going to the market'. Many place nouns can also take the locative **-એ** for 'to/at': **ઘરે** 'home', **શાળાએ** 'to school', **સ્ટેશને** 'to/at the station'.

**-થી** *-thī* means 'from' (also 'by' a means): **અમદાવાદથી** 'from Ahmedabad', **અહીંથી** 'from here', **બસથી** 'by bus'.
**સુધી** means 'up to, as far as, until': **સ્ટેશન સુધી** 'as far as the station'.
**તરફ** means 'towards': **નદી તરફ** 'towards the river'.

Put them together: **અહીંથી ત્યાં સુધી** 'from here to there'.

examples.native: હું રોજ બસથી ઑફિસ જાઉં છું.
examples.roman: huṃ roj basthī ofis jāuṃ chhuṃ.
examples.en: I go to the office by bus every day.
The children have gone to school.
How much is the fare to the station?

examples.native: આ રસ્તો મંદિર તરફ જાય છે.
examples.roman: ā rasto mandir taraf jāy chhe.
examples.en: This road goes towards the temple.

examples.native: વડોદરાથી સુરત સુધી ટ્રેનમાં બે કલાક થાય છે.
examples.roman: Vaḍodarāthī Surat sudhī ṭrenmāṃ be kalāk thāy chhe.
examples.en: From Vadodara to Surat takes two hours by train.

dialogue.title: Taking a rickshaw
dialogue.setting: Lisa flags down an auto-rickshaw outside Ahmedabad's Kalupur railway station.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.en: Bhai, will you go to Law Garden?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.en: Yes, get in. By meter or fixed price?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: ઠીક છે. તમારે ક્યાં ઊતરવું છે?
lines.roman: ṭhīk chhe. tamāre kyāṃ ūtarvuṃ chhe?
lines.en: OK. Where do you want to get off?

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.en: Near Law Garden, opposite the bank.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: પુલ પર બહુ ટ્રાફિક છે. બીજા રસ્તે જઈએ?
lines.roman: pul par bahu ṭrāfik chhe. bījā raste jaīe?
lines.en: There's a lot of traffic on the bridge. Shall we take another road?

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.en: All right. But please drive a bit slowly!

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: આ રહી બેંક. અહીં ઊભી રાખું?
lines.roman: ā rahī beṅk. ahīṃ ūbhī rākhuṃ?
lines.en: Here's the bank. Shall I stop here?

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.native: હા, અહીં બરાબર છે. કેટલા થયા?
lines.roman: hā, ahīṃ barābar chhe. keṭlā thayā?
lines.en: Yes, here is fine. How much is it?

culture: Rickshaw drivers in Ahmedabad are usually addressed as **ભાઈ** or **કાકા**. Directions are given by landmarks rather than street names — a temple, a bank, a famous sweet shop or a **ચાર રસ્તા** — so it's normal to ask several people along the way. **આ રહ્યું / આ રહી** means 'here it is'.

tip.title: Asking the way politely
tip.body:
- Start with **માફ કરજો** 'excuse me', then place + **ક્યાં છે?**: બેંક ક્યાં છે?
- Answers use landmarks: મંદિરની **પાસે** 'near the temple', બેંકની **સામે** 'opposite the bank', દુકાનની **બાજુમાં** 'next to the shop'.
- Before these words the place takes **-ની**: મંદિર**ની** પાસે.

sentences.en: Excuse me, where is the bank?
The bank is opposite the temple.
The hospital is near the station.
The shop is next to the bank.
The market is behind the temple.

sentences.native: માફ કરજો, અહીં હૉસ્પિટલ ક્યાં છે?
sentences.roman: māf karjo, ahīṃ hospiṭal kyāṃ chhe?
sentences.en: Excuse me, where is the hospital around here?
The temple is in the market.

sentences.native: આ રસ્તા પર કોઈ દુકાન છે?
sentences.roman: ā rastā par koī dukān chhe?
sentences.en: Is there a shop on this road?
Does this road go to the station?
Yes, the bank is right here.

tip.title: Telling someone where to go
tip.body:
- Polite (તમે): stem + **-ઓ**: **જાઓ, વળો, આવો**. Use it with adults.
- With a friend (તું): the bare stem: **જા, વળ, આવ**.
- Softer, 'do … when you get there': stem + **-જો**: **વળજો, જજો**.
- 'Don't': **ના** before the verb: ત્યાં **ના** જાઓ.
tip.pattern: સીધા જાઓ · ડાબે વળો · જમણે વળજો

sentences.en: Turn left after the temple.
After the bridge, go straight on.

sentences.native: બીજા ચાર રસ્તા પર ડાબે વળજો.
sentences.roman: bījā chār rastā par ḍābe vaḷjo.
sentences.en: Turn left at the second crossroads.
Turn right here. (to a friend)
Don't go down this lane.

sentences.native: બેંક પછી પહેલી ગલીમાં ડાબે વળજો.
sentences.roman: beṅk pachhī pahelī galīmāṃ ḍābe vaḷjo.
sentences.en: After the bank, turn left into the first lane.
Go straight on at the crossroads.
Don't turn there, go on ahead.
The hospital is on the right.

sentences.native: દુકાન પુલની પાસે, ડાબી બાજુ છે.
sentences.roman: dukān pulnī pāse, ḍābī bāju chhe.
sentences.en: The shop is near the bridge, on the left.

tip.title: From, up to, towards
tip.body:
- Places need **no word for 'to'**: હું બજાર જાઉં છું.
- **-થી** = from (also 'by'): **અહીંથી** 'from here', **બસથી** 'by bus'.
- **સુધી** = up to, as far as: **નદી સુધી**.
- **તરફ** = towards: **સ્ટેશન તરફ**.
- Together: અહીંથી સ્ટેશન સુધી 'from here to the station'.

sentences.en: The bank is close to the temple.

sentences.native: મારું ઘર સ્ટેશનથી બહુ નજીક છે.
sentences.roman: māruṃ ghar sṭeshanthī bahu najīk chhe.
sentences.en: My house is very close to the station.
Go straight as far as the river.

sentences.native: અહીંથી હૉસ્પિટલ સુધી કેટલું દૂર છે?
sentences.roman: ahīṃthī hospiṭal sudhī keṭluṃ dūr chhe?
sentences.en: How far is it from here to the hospital?
I'm heading towards the market.
We're walking towards the river.
Can you walk to the station?
The station isn't far from here.
What's your address?
I don't have a map.

tip.title: Talking to a rickshaw driver
tip.body:
- Call the driver **ભાઈ**, or **કાકા** if he's older.
- Ask with the polite future: **આવશો?** 'will you go (there)?', **કેટલું થશે?** 'how much will it be?'.
- Polite commands: **બેસો** 'get in', **ઊભા રહો** 'stop'. To a friend: **બેસ**, **ઊભો રહે**.

sentences.en: Bhai, will you go to the station?
Get in the rickshaw.
How much will the fare be to the hospital?
Stop near the temple.

sentences.native: અહીં ઊભા ના રહો, આગળ ચલાવો.
sentences.roman: ahīṃ ūbhā nā raho, āgaḷ chalāvo.
sentences.en: Don't stop here, drive on ahead.
Kaka, please drive a bit more slowly.
You sit in front. (to a friend)
Wait! A rickshaw's coming. (to a male friend)
The fare is too high.
How much was the rickshaw fare?

lessons.title: By bus and train

tip.title: મારે … છે — I want to / I have to
tip.body:
- **મારે** + verb in **-વું** + **છે** = I want to / need to: મારે ઊતરવું છે 'I want to get off'.
- With an object, the **-વું** ending follows it: મારે ટિકિટ **લેવી** છે (ટિકિટ is f).
- Ask someone: **તમારે** ક્યાં જવું છે? 'Where do you want to go?'

new: મારે આવતા સ્ટૉપ પર ઊતરવું છે.

sentences.en: I need to go to the station.
I want to buy two tickets.
Which station do you want to get off at?
Which train do you need to take?
I have to get to Ahmedabad today.
We want to go by car.

sentences.native: ભાઈ, બસ ઊભી રાખો, મારે અહીં ઊતરવું છે.
sentences.roman: bhāī, bas ūbhī rākho, māre ahīṃ ūtarvuṃ chhe.
sentences.en: Bhai, stop the bus, I need to get off here.
What time does the train arrive?
The bus stop is near here.
There are a lot of people on the train.
Do you have a ticket?
